# M01R1 kernel reproducibility

M01R1 reopens the M01 NEC98 baseline build only. It resolves a reproducibility
defect found when the native x86-64 prerequisite build for M02 was run. No
PC-88VA implementation or bootability claim is part of this work.

## Identity and preserved evidence

The accepted parent was `096d9ba3fc5f0239822ac71e697bffd34c8a86d4`. The
native x86-64 M02 prerequisite run `33248650931` exposed the drift but
retained manifests rather than binaries. A bounded diagnostic-only native
rerun at `33288083356` retained the fresh pair before cleanup. Both accepted
and fresh pairs were regular, non-symlink files of 83774 bytes, and each pair
was internally byte-identical.

| evidence | `kernel.sys` and `KWC8616.sys` SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| accepted M01 | `89534be7b9e8646fc0d5eabe8292f7fe86142192cbb22115fc469b253afb5705` |
| native x86-64 drift | `3e0ff13184a9fed3a9eb30ab9ac38aec50e529f5cea2ddb3edd7353747aad408` |

The accepted committed evidence digests were components lock
`291490d59e62280e617a5107d11363cfecfbd7238815105b81dd5f8468a247bd`,
toolchain lock
`39c5b3052d71463235a26e8704ab54c1fedb51ee75bb4efb55e6229391a95162`, M01
build contract
`85a3a9a96b4b5fb4f4d1d90f836c97eade24a639de4aa0f908640ca91057759c`, and
M01 golden
`756be74a0c72f9150173e053812094de334a69dc193b627e06421536598d22fb`.

## Root cause

The primary classification is **compiled-source drift**. The only binary
difference between the accepted pair and the native drift pair is the byte at
offset `21141` (`[21141,21142)`). It changes from `0x38` to `0x39`, and the
bounded printable windows identify the embedded strings as:

```text
accepted: [compiled Aug 28 2026]
fresh:    [compiled Aug 29 2026]
```

There is no MZ header in these flat kernel outputs, and no other binary range
differs. `KWC8616.sys` is an output alias, not independent kernel evidence.

`components/fdkernel/hdr/version.h` used the compiler's raw `__DATE__` in the
KVS version/banner data. `components/fdkernel/nec98/kernel/globals.h` includes
that header; the NEC98 kernel makefile's `INITHEADERS` path compiles it into
the kernel objects, including `main.obj`, then the kernel link and `exeflat`
path carry the value into `kernel.sys`. This connects the exact source input to
the one differing output byte. The source archive and compiler/tool identities
were otherwise locked.

The same-day M01 comparison missed this because its two isolated runs were
performed on one date and did not record object or generated-input identities.
The native x86-64 run on the following date exposed the date transition.

The diagnostic census also found a secondary generated-input issue. The four
FAT headers generated by `sys/bin2c.c` had identical bytes but inherited
different source-time mtimes, producing eight debug/include-record byte
differences in `sys/sys.obj` at offsets `148, 191, 197, 241, 247, 290, 296,
339`. This did not change `SYS.COM`, but it violated the required complete
object-manifest invariant and was fixed in the same narrowly scoped child
commit. The linker response file and ordered link inputs were identical. Map
timestamp and link-duration differences were diagnostics-only and not link
inputs. The accepted object tree was not retained, so object-level comparison
to the accepted build is unavailable; binary localization plus fresh isolated
object/link evidence establishes the causal path.

## Fix

Child commit `6523acdb87f4665e6068ea331859885267242005` on the dedicated
fdkernel branch makes the version date an opt-in `KERNEL_BUILD_DATE` macro,
while retaining the upstream `__DATE__` fallback outside the M01
configuration. The parent M01 harness derives the date in UTC from the
committed fdkernel `source_date_epoch` (`1787814827`, `Aug 27 2026`) using
repository-owned Python code and passes it through a read-only staged WMake
configuration. No host `date`, clock modification, compiler replacement,
optimization change, post-link patch, hard-coded output hash, or
`libfaketime` assumption is used.

The same child commit makes `bin2c` honor a validated `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` for
generated-header mtimes. Its default behavior remains available when the
variable is absent. The M01 container records source inputs, generated inputs,
objects, compiler/build command lines, response-file order, link inputs,
source epoch, and timezone in bounded diagnostics.

## Regression invariant and candidate golden

The M01R1 regression gate requires two isolated M01 runs to have identical
complete artifact manifests, object/source/generated-input content maps,
ordered response/link inputs, deterministic generated-header mtimes, and
kernel aliases. It also runs the modified `bin2c` in different working
directories with different source mtimes under `TZ=UTC` and `TZ=Asia/Tokyo`,
and rejects malformed epochs. The fixed output contains exactly one
`[compiled Aug 27 2026]` stamp. Literal cross-day execution is not claimed.

The resulting candidate kernel pair remains 83774 bytes and has SHA-256
`3ebddb01abe5e39f16d27439836be283c57d454f012d3c990f01fa8a2b14101d`.
All ten M01 artifacts were accounted for, and non-kernel artifact identities
remained unchanged. The new fdkernel source archive is
`b9cbb7d40958a5ca0c6c49217464dba73b4bcb4dbe04e764648e0b3d8f66892d`; the
toolchain lock is unchanged. After local regression and two-run comparison,
the new M01 golden was explicitly enrolled with SHA-256
`6fcfe834f90ffc602589ddc63b50d90eba33bbc1802b6bff3c9ef6b9d397c7c3`,
superseding `756be74a0c72f9150173e053812094de334a69dc193b627e06421536598d22fb`
because the corrected deterministic input is a third, reproducible output.
Ordinary verification does not rewrite the golden.

Evidence is limited to the retained accepted/native binary pairs, native
manifests and maps, and fresh local object/link diagnostics; no private or
generated binary diagnostic tree is committed. M02 remains isolated and is
not resumed here. Root repository license selection remains deferred.
